programs.name: Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers (PCAFC)
programs.agency: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VHA Caregiver Support Program)
programs.eligibility: Veteran must have a VA disability rating of 70% or higher (or be unable to perform daily activities due to a serious injury), be enrolled in VA health care, and need at least 6 months of continuous, in-person personal care services. The caregiver must be 18+ and either related to the veteran or live with them full-time.
programs.coverage: The designated Primary Family Caregiver receives a monthly stipend, plus CHAMPVA health coverage (if not otherwise covered), mental health counseling, financial/legal planning assistance, and at least 30 days of respite care per year. The stipend is not a fixed national figure — it is based on the federal GS-4, step 1 annual rate for the veteran's locality, divided by 12, times a level multiplier (0.625 or 1.00).
programs.notes: Apply via VA Form 10-10CG. Call the Caregiver Support Line at 1-855-260-3274 to be matched with a local Caregiver Support Coordinator first.

programs.name: Program of General Caregiver Support Services (PGCSS)
programs.agency: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VHA Caregiver Support Program)
programs.eligibility: No disability-rating threshold. Available to any caregiver of a veteran enrolled in VA health care and receiving personal care services, as long as the veteran agrees to receive care from that caregiver. The caregiver need not be a relative or live with the veteran.
programs.coverage: Skills training and coaching, peer-support mentoring, support groups, telephone support, online self-care programs, and referrals. No monthly stipend and no enhanced respite care (those are PCAFC-only).
programs.notes: No formal application — contact your VA facility's Caregiver Support Coordinator or call 1-855-260-3274. A good entry point when the veteran doesn't meet PCAFC's 70% threshold.

programs.name: VA Caregiver Support Line
programs.agency: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VHA Caregiver Support Program)
programs.eligibility: Open to all caregivers and family members of veterans; no enrollment required to call.
programs.coverage: Toll-free phone support at 1-855-260-3274, staffed by licensed professionals (Mon–Fri, 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. ET). Provides referrals, emotional support, and help enrolling in PCAFC or PGCSS.
programs.notes: As of April 2024 this line also handles the calls formerly taken by Coaching Into Care, making it the single front door for both caregiver questions and help getting a veteran into care.

programs.name: Veterans Crisis Line
programs.eligibility: Any veteran, service member (including National Guard/Reserve), and their family or friends. No VA enrollment or benefits required.
programs.coverage: Free, confidential, 24/7 crisis support: call 988 then press 1, text 838255, or chat online. Responders can connect callers to local VA resources and emergency services.
programs.notes: You don't have to be in suicidal crisis to call — it's also for stress, sleep, relationship, or transition problems. Callers control what personal information they share.

programs.name: Vet Centers (Readjustment Counseling)
programs.agency: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VHA Readjustment Counseling Service)
programs.eligibility: Veterans and service members who served in a combat zone/area of hostility, experienced military sexual trauma (MST), provided mortuary/drone services, or meet other criteria — plus their families. Bereaved family members of those who died on active duty are also eligible.
programs.coverage: Free individual, group, marriage, and family counseling; MST counseling; bereavement counseling; and readjustment/PTSD/depression counseling. Delivered at community Vet Centers (and mobile Vet Centers), separate from VA medical centers.
programs.notes: Vet Center records are kept confidential and separate from VA medical/benefits files, lowering the barrier for veterans wary of a formal paper trail. The 24/7 Vet Center Call Center is 1-877-927-8387.

programs.name: VA Mental Health Services
programs.agency: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (Veterans Health Administration)
programs.eligibility: Veterans enrolled in VA health care can access the full range of services; some services (MST-related care, readjustment counseling, crisis care) are available even without enrollment.
programs.coverage: Assessment and treatment for PTSD, depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, suicidal thoughts, MST, and substance use — including individual/group/couples/family therapy, medication, inpatient and outpatient care, telehealth, peer support, and same-day services.
programs.notes: You can get same-day mental health help by walking into any VA medical center or calling 1-877-222-8387; you don't have to wait for a scheduled appointment.

programs.name: Military Sexual Trauma (MST) Care
programs.agency: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (Veterans Health Administration)
programs.eligibility: Veterans and most former service members — including those with an Other Than Honorable discharge or who served fewer than two years — regardless of disability rating or VA health-care enrollment. No need to have reported the MST when it happened or to prove it occurred.
programs.coverage: Free treatment for any physical or mental health condition related to MST: psychological assessment, individual and group therapy, medication evaluation, and related physical health care. Available to all genders.
programs.notes: Ask for the MST Coordinator at your nearest VA facility (or use a Vet Center) — they can arrange care discreetly.

programs.name: Substance Use Disorder Treatment
programs.agency: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (Veterans Health Administration)
programs.eligibility: Veterans enrolled in VA health care; combat veterans without VA benefits can also access free counseling through Vet Centers.
programs.coverage: Medically managed detox; medication-assisted treatment (e.g., buprenorphine for opioids, nicotine replacement for tobacco); outpatient counseling; residential treatment; marital/family therapy; peer support; and integrated treatment for co-occurring PTSD/depression.
programs.notes: Start by asking any VA primary care provider for a substance-use screening and referral — you don't need a separate specialty intake to begin.

programs.name: Bereavement Counseling (Vet Centers)
programs.agency: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VHA Readjustment Counseling Service)
programs.eligibility: Family members of Armed Forces personnel who died in service; Reserve/National Guard members who died while on duty; family members of veterans who were receiving Vet Center services at the time of an unexpected death or death during hospice care; and families of veterans or service members who died by suicide.
programs.coverage: Free outreach, counseling, and referral services for surviving spouses, children, and parents, provided through community Vet Centers.
programs.notes: Request it through any Vet Center via the 24/7 Vet Center Call Center at 1-877-927-8387.
